title: Texto, Unicode y expresiones regulares
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only concepts marked USABLE in the effective prior ledger count as learned.

roadmap_expectation.T1: code points, Unicode normalization, casefold, tildes, ñ, particles and compound surnames
roadmap_expectation.T2: split/join/search/replace; names, emails and phones without overvalidation
roadmap_expectation.T3: regex patterns, groups, anchors, compilation, extraction and validation limits
roadmap_expectation.T4: normalized equality, token similarity, FP/FN and evidence preservation
roadmap_expectation.gate: pipeline conserves raw and normalized, records transforms and handles two surnames without assuming a universal convention

live_site.note: Public fetch returned DisabledError in this environment; no exact hydrated-render parity claim is made.

adversarial_review.most_likely_beginner_failure: The learner confuses normalization with identity resolution: the prose says two textual forms can be 'the same person', the name parser overcommits on surname positions, and later safeguards cannot fully undo that first mental model.
adversarial_review.suspected_hidden_prerequisite: Function wrapper semantics, exceptions, imports, raw-string notation and some compact typing/generator syntax are used as explanatory machinery before they are usable.
adversarial_review.most_likely_misconception: That a high text-similarity score or a successful heuristic parse carries more identity evidence than it actually does, and that empty/low-information inputs can safely receive ordinary similarity scores.

confirmed_findings.evidence: CP-N1-B/gate remain learner-facing internal identifiers without a stable plain-language expansion.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The surrounding text is understandable but the named deliverable remains opaque.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot tell whether CP-N1-B is a project increment, exercise, file, runtime gate or assessment.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The code appears in the promise and closing criterion, so ambiguity affects goal orientation.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Expand once as 'CP-N1-B, el segundo incremento del proyecto acumulativo del Nivel 1' and then reuse the code.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The theory repeatedly wraps examples in def s07_th_N(): ...; the effective S05 ledger left function definition and argument/binding mechanics PARTIAL rather than USABLE.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Only concepts marked USABLE may be assumed; return is usable, full function-definition/call trace is not.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Every new text/Unicode concept is hidden behind a function-definition/call wrapper unrelated to the concept being taught.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: A learner may understand NFC or split but still fail to predict whether and when the indented code executes because the wrapper itself is not mastered.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Worked examples should isolate the target concept rather than test an unresolved prerequisite.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use top-level statements for early S07 theory examples; introduce helper functions only where a reusable normalization function is itself pedagogically useful and trace its call explicitly.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Examples use import unicodedata and import re; the prose names stdlib modules but does not explain what import does. Module/import mechanics are canonically later.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Required standard-library tools appear through unexplained syntax.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can infer that unicodedata/re are magic names built into every program or that import installs packages.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: S07 legitimately needs these modules, but a one-sentence bridge is enough to avoid a false model.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add: 'unicodedata/re son módulos incluidos con Python; import nombre hace disponibles sus funciones en este archivo; no instala nada.'

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson says 'Ma. del Carmen es la misma persona que María del Carmen' before later insisting that text similarity is only evidence and never proof of identity.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No entity-resolution authority or external identity evidence.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A textual abbreviation is stated as an identity fact rather than a possible representation.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can conclude that recognizable abbreviation expansion is sufficient to assert two records belong to one person.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: It directly contradicts the course's own preservation rule that textual similarity cannot prove identity/kinship/fraud.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Replace with 'Ma. del Carmen puede ser una abreviatura de María del Carmen; el texto por sí solo no demuestra que dos registros pertenezcan a la misma persona.'

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose correctly says particles such as de/del/de la can belong to names or surnames, then teaches 'últimos dos tokens = apellidos si hay tres o más'. For 'María Pérez de la Cruz' that heuristic produces given='María Pérez de', apellido1='la', apellido2='Cruz'.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Strings/tokens are being taught here; no authoritative name schema is available.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The canonical parser fails exactly on compound-surname particles the lesson says it handles and does not route those ambiguous cases to review.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can split 'de la Cruz' or another compound surname into semantically wrong fields while believing the Latin-American model was handled safely.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The roadmap outcome explicitly promises particles and two surnames without assuming a universal convention.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Do not infer surname boundaries from token count alone. Teach a bounded synthetic schema where fields are known, or keep the full normalized name and mark automated component parsing as review when particles make the boundary ambiguous.

confirmed_findings.evidence: normalize_email calls raw.strip().casefold() on the entire address. SMTP specifies that the mailbox local-part must be treated as case-sensitive while the domain is case-insensitive; casefold can also expand characters such as ß -> ss.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S07 is responsible for defining what text normalization may safely change.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The normalizer alters the local-part without a domain/provider-specific policy authorizing that semantic change.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Distinct local-parts can be collapsed into one normalized identifier, violating the lesson's own rule to preserve meaning while normalizing representation.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Email normalization is a concrete business boundary; destructive normalization can create false matches.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Preserve local-part case by default; normalize/casefold the domain separately. If a specific provider policy permits local-part folding, make that policy explicit and retain raw.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose says a nonconforming email goes to review; normalize_email raises ValueError, and the theory provides no caller that catches that exception and routes it to review. Exception flow is not yet usable and is canonically taught later.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The behavior promised by prose (review) is not the behavior shown by the code (uncaught exception).
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: A learner can believe raising ValueError automatically means the case was safely queued for human review, when execution instead aborts unless another layer catches it.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: This conflates error signaling with recovery/routing and repeats the exception leak seen in earlier sections.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Either return an explicit review result using already-taught structures, or teach one bounded exception-signaling sentence and defer catching/routing until the later exception section; do not claim review unless shown.

confirmed_findings.evidence: normalize_phone_pe keeps characters where str.isdigit() is true, and the DNI regex uses \d{8}. Python Unicode semantics include non-ASCII digits; str.isdigit also includes some compatibility digits. Executions retained Arabic-Indic/fullwidth/superscript digits and re.fullmatch(r'\d{8}', '١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨') returned True.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: This is the Unicode lesson; the learner should be told when character classes are Unicode-wide versus ASCII/business-specific.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The code silently broadens 'dígitos de teléfono/DNI peruano' beyond the ASCII 0-9 symbols the domain example appears to intend.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: A learner can accept a synthetic DNI or phone string containing unexpected Unicode digits while believing the code enforces 0-9.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The course is explicitly teaching both Unicode and validation boundaries; this is a high-value place to distinguish semantic character classes from domain alphabets.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: If the course contract requires ASCII digits, use [0-9]{8} for the synthetic DNI and filter with ch in '0123456789' for the phone; alternatively explicitly state that Unicode decimal digits are accepted and normalize them deliberately.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The heading promises split/join/search/replace and the prose lists find/startswith, but theory never explains that str.find returns an index or -1. Because -1 is truthy and 0 is falsy, using if s.find(x): produces wrong decisions at both the first-position and missing cases.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Truthiness is USABLE from S03; string searching is new here.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A search API is named without its return contract, despite its return value interacting dangerously with previously learned truthiness.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner may write if texto.find('Lima'): and treat a match at index 0 as false while treating 'not found' (-1) as true.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: This is a predictable novice failure created by combining two course concepts.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Teach 'needle in text' for yes/no membership; if find is taught, state explicitly: returns 0..n-1 when found and -1 when absent, so compare against -1 rather than using it as a boolean.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Regex examples use r'...' and T3-B calls it a raw string, but the lesson never explains the r prefix or why regex patterns commonly use it.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A new Python string-literal form is introduced at the same time as regex metacharacters.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can attribute backslash behavior to regex when part of the behavior belongs to Python string parsing, or copy doubled backslashes inconsistently.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Regex already carries high intrinsic load; one microdefinition removes an avoidable layer of ambiguity.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add: 'r
es un raw string de Python: conserva las barras invertidas para que el motor regex reciba \d, \b, etc. sin duplicarlas en la mayoría de patrones.'

confirmed_findings.evidence: The outcome promises anchors ^$, but the prose mainly teaches fullmatch and the code combines ^...$ with fullmatch, so the learner cannot tell which mechanism enforces whole-string coverage. The symbols are never explicitly mapped to start/end.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Two boundary mechanisms are introduced simultaneously without isolating their responsibilities.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can believe fullmatch requires ^/$ or use anchors mechanically without understanding them.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Boundary semantics are central to the advertised difference between validation and extraction.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: First teach fullmatch with r'[0-9]{8}'. Then separately define ^ as start and $ as end using search/match examples, noting that anchors are redundant in the preceding fullmatch example.

confirmed_findings.evidence: token_jaccard returns 1.0 when both token sets are empty and 0.0 when only one is empty, while the opening/T4-B policy says missing evidence must go to review rather than receive an invented conclusion.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Falsy/empty distinctions and fail-closed review policy are already part of the course thread.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: No-evidence cases receive ordinary numeric similarity scores, including the maximum possible score for empty-vs-empty.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Two blank names can appear maximally similar, or one blank name can look like a confident no-match, instead of being recognized as insufficient evidence.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: This directly violates the lesson's safety contract and can bias downstream review thresholds.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Return no score (for example None plus reason='sin tokens') when either side has no usable tokens, and route that condition to review separately from similarity.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Jaccard is defined over sets but the lesson does not explicitly state that sets discard order and repeated tokens. The implemented score gives 1.0 for 'Juan Perez' vs 'Perez Juan' and for 'Ana Ana' vs 'Ana'.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner receives the formula without the most important representational information loss caused by converting tokens to a set.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: A score of 1.0 can be interpreted as textual equivalence even when word order or repetition differs.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The course repeatedly warns score != identity; explaining what the score itself discards is part of that warning.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one sentence and one counterexample: 'Jaccard de conjuntos ignora orden y repeticiones; 1.0 significa mismos tokens únicos, no mismo texto ni misma persona.'

confirmed_findings.evidence: The table assigns score 0.9 to 'José Pérez' vs 'Jose Perez' immediately after defining token Jaccard as the section's similarity score. Under the canonical tokens() implementation those sets have no intersection and Jaccard is 0.0 because NFC/casefold do not remove accents.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner has just been taught one explicit score formula.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The next example silently substitutes an unexplained score from another method or an invented number.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot reproduce the displayed evidence and may infer that Jaccard somehow treats accented/unaccented tokens as nearly equal.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: A central principle of the lesson is that evidence must be auditable; a fabricated score is the opposite.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Compute every score using token_jaccard in the example, or label a different metric explicitly and teach it before using it. For José/Jose under current Jaccard, show 0.0 and explain why accent removal is not part of the pipeline.

confirmed_findings.evidence: FP/FN are defined as cases where the system 'should' or 'should not' match, but theory never introduces the reference label/ground truth needed to know that. The example contains score and decision only, not expected_match.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No statistics or supervised-evaluation model is assumed.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner is asked to label FP/FN without the external truth value that makes those labels meaningful.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can call a high-score pair a false positive based on intuition rather than comparing a prediction against an independently established synthetic truth label.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: Without ground truth, FP/FN cannot be operationally computed or audited.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Introduce a synthetic expected_match label supplied independently of the text score; define FP/FN as prediction versus that reference. Keep real sensitive identity decisions outside the synthetic exercise.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The opening says every exercise uses raw/normalized/transforms and the closing claims each transformation leaves an auditable trace, but none of the theory code blocks actually constructs a record that preserves raw, normalized and an ordered transforms list together.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: list/dict are USABLE from S06, so the theory can demonstrate this contract directly.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The central auditability artifact is described but not demonstrated before practice.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can normalize text correctly yet overwrite raw or fail to record which transformation changed the value, while believing the theory already taught the audit contract.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The roadmap gate explicitly requires raw + normalized + recorded transformations.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one small theory example that starts from raw, applies NFC/space collapse/case policy step by step, appends named transforms, and returns/prints all three fields without overwriting raw.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson glosses code points as numbers Unicode assigns to each 'carácter' while its own é example demonstrates that one user-perceived character can be represented by multiple code points.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The everyday word 'carácter' is doing two jobs: visible grapheme and Unicode code point.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can conclude one visible character always equals one code point, then fail to understand combining marks, emoji sequences or length differences.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: S07 exists specifically to repair the assumption that visible text maps one-to-one to stored units.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say: 'Un code point es un número asignado por Unicode a una unidad abstracta; un símbolo visible puede estar formado por uno o varios code points.'

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose calls exactly-one-@, nonempty local/domain and no spaces a 'comprobación modesta pero completa', while SMTP syntax permits quoted local-parts and the course itself warns against claiming full email validity.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner only needs a bounded intake policy, not RFC-complete mailbox syntax.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The word 'completa' turns a deliberately narrow business subset into an apparent general email-validity rule.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner may later reject standards-valid addresses as malformed instead of recognizing that the course intentionally supports a restricted subset and routes others to review.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The advertised lesson goal is specifically 'sin sobrevalidación'.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Rename it 'regla mínima del laboratorio' and state that it defines the subset accepted automatically; other forms may be valid but should be reviewed rather than declared invalid.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The figure introduces bytes, decode, UTF-8 vs Latin-1 and mojibake inside the str-method subtopic, while the lesson repeatedly states encoding/decoding is taught in S08.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A future-stage failure mechanism appears visually before the learner has the concepts needed to explain it, interrupting the current str-operation thread.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can conflate Unicode normalization of an existing str with decoding bytes into str and expect NFC to repair encoding corruption.
confirmed_findings.why_it_matters: The closing bridge to S08 already handles this transition more appropriately.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Move the encoding-chain figure to the S07 closing bridge or S08 opening; keep T2-A focused on operations on already-decoded str values.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: NFC removes accents or makes Jose equal José.
rejected_findings.reason: The lesson correctly says NFC changes representation, not meaning/spelling, and explicitly asks the learner to explain that boundary.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: casefold is always wrong for Spanish because lower is enough.
rejected_findings.reason: The lesson accurately describes casefold as a broader caseless-comparison policy and correctly notes that lower/casefold often coincide for ñ. The email-specific use is a separate defect.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: Using str methods before regex is technically wrong or simplistic.
rejected_findings.reason: The staged preference is pedagogically and technically sound; literal operations should not be replaced by regex merely for sophistication.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: zip/set/list knowledge is illegitimate in S07.
rejected_findings.reason: list/dict/set are usable from S06. Only concepts left PARTIAL or risky remain non-creditable.
The distinction is technically correct; the issue is only the simultaneous unexplained anchor notation.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: Python re provides a built-in timeout parameter that the lesson omitted.
rejected_findings.reason: For the target Python stdlib re API, the lesson's warning that it lacks a timeout parameter is correct.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: Jaccard itself is inappropriate and must be removed.
rejected_findings.reason: As a transparent weak signal for human review, Jaccard is reasonable. The defects are empty-input handling, unspoken set information loss and inconsistent fabricated scores.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: The lesson should parse every Latin-American name perfectly.
rejected_findings.reason: No universal parser is required. The defect is that the chosen heuristic contradicts the stated particle limitation while still claiming to model those cases.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Escribe José dos veces... una versión guarda la é... otra e seguida de tilde...
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could overstate Unicode equality or decoding.
paragraph_reviews.defense: It accurately creates the canonical-equivalence problem and connects it to record matching.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Poner de acuerdo esas dos formas... normalización Unicode... str antes de regex.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could be dogmatic about str before regex.
paragraph_reviews.defense: The staged decision rule is useful and does not claim regex is never appropriate.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Ma. del Carmen es la misma persona que María del Carmen... parecido es una señal.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Identity assertion contradicts later evidence-only rule.
paragraph_reviews.defense: The paragraph tries to motivate variant spellings, but the categorical identity language cannot be defended from text alone.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Comparar nombres es difícil: 'Ma. del Carmen' puede ser una abreviatura de 'María del Carmen', pero el texto por sí solo no demuestra que dos registros pertenezcan a la misma persona. La similitud es una señal para revisión, no una conclusión de identidad.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: raw... normalized... transforms... lista de lo que se hizo.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Central contract may be only declarative.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Definitions are clear, but later theory never shows the three fields together.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Mantener el párrafo; añadir inmediatamente un worked example mínimo que conserve raw y construya normalized + transforms sin sobrescribir el original.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: conservar raw → normalizar → comparar → reunir evidencia → decidir/review.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could imply automated identity decision.
paragraph_reviews.defense: It explicitly includes evidence and review and is consistent with fail-closed intent.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: schema... no cuadre... no completar campo... revisión.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Schema is new jargon.
paragraph_reviews.defense: The sentence immediately microdefines schema as fields + types and gives the consequence.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Bloque de referencia. Orden...
paragraph_reviews.attack: Meta text might be unnecessary.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Optional reference orientation is transparent and harmless.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: T1 Unicode... T2 str... T3 regex... T4 similitud.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could overload terms before definitions.
paragraph_reviews.defense: As optional map, terms are labels rather than required mastery.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: I Do / We Do / You Do...
paragraph_reviews.attack: Refers to excluded surfaces.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Does not externalize essential theory by itself; no practice audit performed.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Criterio de cierre CP-N1-B... raw/normalized/transforms.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Opaque project code and theory lacks complete worked example.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Criterion itself is aligned with roadmap.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Criterio de cierre (CP-N1-B, segundo incremento del proyecto acumulativo del Nivel 1): un normalizador que conserva raw, produce normalized y registra transforms en orden, acompañado por la evidencia usada para comparar.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Solo datos sintéticos... nunca parentesco... S08/S12.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could be repetitive.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Repetition serves a safety boundary and preserves scope.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Python 3 str es Unicode... ord/chr... NFC/NFD...
paragraph_reviews.attack: Visible character versus code point is conflated.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Core example is correct but needs one precision sentence.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Python 3 str representa texto Unicode. Un code point es un número asignado por Unicode a una unidad abstracta; un símbolo visible puede usar uno o varios code points. Por eso una é puede aparecer como U+00E9 o como e + una marca combinante.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: unicodedata.normalize NFC... stdlib str/unicodedata/re.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Uses importable modules without import model.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Modules are necessary here, so a microdefinition is enough.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Antes de usarlo: unicodedata es un módulo incluido con Python; import unicodedata hace disponibles sus operaciones en este archivo y no instala nada. normalize('NFC', s) unifica formas canónicamente equivalentes antes de comparar o tokenizar.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: casefold política canónica... lower... pipeline NFC → strip/collapse → casefold.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could overstate casefold globally.
paragraph_reviews.defense: For generic caseless text matching the explanation is sound; the email-specific application is audited separately.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Predice code points... NFC cambia comparación pero no corrige nombre mal escrito.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could confuse normalization with correction.
paragraph_reviews.defense: It explicitly draws that boundary correctly.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: En Perú y Latam... dos apellidos... raw siempre.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Regional naming pattern could be universalized.
paragraph_reviews.defense: It says common rather than universal and explicitly rejects US-only forcing.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: partículas de/del/de la... parser suave... últimos dos tokens = apellidos.
paragraph_reviews.attack: The heuristic contradicts the particle warning.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Review on too-few tokens does not catch compound surnames with enough tokens.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Las partículas pueden pertenecer al nombre o al apellido, así que el número de tokens no basta para localizar automáticamente dos apellidos. Conserva el nombre completo normalizado; separa componentes solo cuando el formulario o una fuente confiable ya proporciona esa estructura. Si la frontera es ambigua, envía a review.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: María del Carmen Quispe Huamán → given + dos apellidos.
paragraph_reviews.attack: One successful synthetic case may look like a general parser contract.
paragraph_reviews.defense: It is explicitly synthetic but follows the unsafe heuristic.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Usa María del Carmen Quispe Huamán solo como caso donde la estructura de campos sea conocida de antemano; no lo presentes como prueba de que la misma regla separa cualquier nombre latinoamericano.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Prueba heurística... dos tokens → review.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Only tests too-few-token ambiguity, not particle ambiguity.
paragraph_reviews.defense: The review instinct is good but the trigger is incomplete.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Prueba también un apellido compuesto como 'de la Cruz'. Si más de una segmentación es razonable, conserva el nombre completo y marca review; no elijas una frontera solo porque el número de tokens encaja.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: strip, split, join, replace, find, startswith antes de regex.
paragraph_reviews.attack: find is named without its return contract and creates a truthiness trap.
paragraph_reviews.defense: The tool-order principle is good but incomplete.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Antes de regex usa operaciones literales. Para una pregunta sí/no prefiere 'texto in s' o startswith. Si necesitas la posición, find devuelve el índice 0..n-1 y -1 cuando no encuentra; no uses directamente ese entero como condición booleana.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: join(split())... split(',') CSV-like simple... S08 csv/pathlib.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could encourage hand-rolled CSV parsing.
paragraph_reviews.defense: The paragraph explicitly limits split(',') to simple unquoted cases and defers real CSV to S08.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: replace literal... documenta transforms y conserva raw.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Trace policy is not shown in code.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Prose is correct; issue is the missing integrated artifact.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Mantener la regla y hacer que el ejemplo adjunte 'collapse_spaces' y 'replace_abbrev' a transforms mientras raw permanece intacto.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: literal vs delimitador vs forma variable.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could oversimplify tool choice.
paragraph_reviews.defense: As an introductory decision heuristic it is clear and bounded.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: email strip + casefold... exactamente un @... ningún espacio... modesta pero completa.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Full-address casefold changes local-part semantics; 'complete' overclaims a restricted policy.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Routing uncommon forms to review can be legitimate, but the current normalization and wording are unsafe.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Para el laboratorio define una regla mínima, no una definición completa de email: recorta espacios externos, separa local y dominio y normaliza solo el dominio para comparación. Conserva el local-part tal como fue escrito salvo que una política específica autorice cambiarlo. Formas que el curso no soporte pueden ir a review sin declararlas inválidas.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Teléfono PE... extrae dígitos... +51... solo dígitos.
paragraph_reviews.attack: isdigit accepts a broader Unicode class than ASCII phone digits.
paragraph_reviews.defense: The normalization goal is reasonable but the character policy is unstated.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Si el contrato del laboratorio exige dígitos ASCII, conserva únicamente caracteres de '0123456789'. No uses isdigit como sinónimo de 0–9 sin explicar que Unicode contiene otras clases de dígitos.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Nombre contacto... title-case cosmética... score evidencia.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could normalize names destructively.
paragraph_reviews.defense: It explicitly labels title-case cosmetic/policy-dependent and preserves evidence-only matching.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: Jaccard = intersección/unión sobre sets... score 0.67.
paragraph_reviews.attack: Set conversion discards token order/repetition and empty evidence is not bounded.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Formula is correct but representation losses are omitted.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Jaccard compara conjuntos de tokens: ignora el orden y cuántas veces se repite un token. Por eso 1.0 significa 'mismos tokens únicos', no 'mismo texto'. Si cualquiera de los lados queda sin tokens, no calcules un score ordinario: marca evidencia insuficiente y envía a review.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: igualdad exacta, muestra intersección/unión antes de dividir.
paragraph_reviews.attack: No-evidence path needs to happen before division as a separate state.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Making sets visible is excellent scaffolding.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Muestra A, B, A∩B y A∪B. Si A o B está vacío, detente: no hay evidencia suficiente para un score comparable. Si ambos tienen tokens, recién divide y explica qué información descartó el uso de conjuntos.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: FP sistema dice match y no debería; FN debería y no hizo.
paragraph_reviews.attack: 'Debería' requires an independent reference label that is not defined.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Informal definitions are directionally correct but not operationally auditable.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Para hablar de FP/FN necesitas una etiqueta de referencia independiente del score. En datos sintéticos, define expected_match de antemano. FP = el sistema predice match cuando expected_match es false; FN = predice no_match cuando expected_match es true.

paragraph_reviews.current_content_excerpt: evidence raw_a/raw_b/score/decision/reason... fail-closed.

paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Conserva raw_a/raw_b y, cuando haya tokens suficientes, score + reason. Si falta evidencia, registra score=None, reason='evidencia insuficiente' y decision='review'; no conviertas ausencia en 0.0 o 1.0.
